'''''Victoria cruziana''''' ('''Santa Cruz water lily''', '''water platter''', '''yrupe''', synonym '''''Victoria argentina''''' [[Hermann Carl Conrad Burmeister|Burmeist.]]) is a tropical species of flowering plant, of the [[Nymphaeaceae]] family of water lilies native to [[South America]], primarily Brazil, [[Bolivia]], [[Argentina]] and [[Paraguay]].

==Description==
The plant is a popular water garden plant in botanical gardens where its very large leaves can reach their fullest, up to 2 m wide with a thick rim up to 20 cm high,<ref name="Kew">{{cite web|title=Victoria cruziana (Santa Cruz waterlily)|url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:605778-1|website=Kew Gardens|publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens| access-date=24 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Nash|first=Helen|title=Complete guide to water garden plants|year=2003|publisher=Sterling Publishing|location=New York|isbn=1402709544|pages=70–71|author2=Steve Stroupe }}</ref> although rims up to 23 cm have been recorded.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.watergardenersinternational.org/journal/2-1/francois/page1.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080830030941/http://www.watergardenersinternational.org/journal/2-1/francois/page1.html | url-status=usurped | archive-date=30 August 2008 | title= Mammoth Victoria crusiana |  last= VanAvondt | first= Francois | date= n.d. | access-date= 3 March 2015 }}</ref> It can be grown in cooler waters than its sisters within the genus, the more familiar giant waterlily, ''[[Victoria amazonica]]'' and the recently discovered ''[[Victoria boliviana]]''.<ref name=Lamprecht>{{cite journal|last=Lamprecht|first=I|author2=E. Schmolz |author3=S. Hilsberg |author4=S. Schlegel |title=A tropical water lily with strong thermogenic behaviour— thermometric and thermographic investigations on Victoria cruziana|journal=Thermochimica Acta|year=2002|volume=382|issue=1–2|pages=199–210|doi=10.1016/s0040-6031(01)00734-1}}</ref> A 25 cm diameter flower blooms for two days, arising from the underwater bud, as a white flower that turns to a deep pink on the second and final day of its bloom. ''V. cruziana'' is a [[Thermogenesis|thermogenetic]] or heat-producing plant.<ref>Lamprecht, I., et al. A Tropical Water Lily with Strong Thermogenic Behaviour—Thermometric and Thermographic Investigations on ''Victoria cruziana''. Thermochimica Acta, vol. 382, no. 1-2, 2002, pp. 199–210., doi:10.1016/s0040-6031(01)00734-1.</ref><ref>Wu, Q., et al. Relationship between the Flavonoid Composition and Flower Colour Variation in Victoria. Plant Biology, vol. 20, no. 4, 2018, pp. 674–681., doi:10.1111/plb.12835.</ref> The floral [[Stigma (botany)|stigma]] are attached to a cup that is protected by spines, and the floral cup begins heating up in the bud, then, as the flower opens, it releases a strong sweet scent to attract pollinating [[beetles]] of the genus ''[[Cyclocephala]]'' of the family ''[[Scarabaeidae]]'',<ref>{{cite book |last= Proctor | first= Michael | last2= Yeo | first2= Peter | last3= Lack | first3= Andrew | date= 1996 | title= The Natural History of Pollination | location= Portland | publisher= Timber Press | page= 310 | isbn= 0-88192-353-2}}</ref> then continues to provide heat to the flower while the beetles are pollinating.<ref name=Lamprecht /><ref name=Lamprecht2>{{cite journal|last=Lamprecht|first=I |author2=E. Schmolz |author3=L. Blanco |author4=C.M. Romero|title=Flower ovens: thermal investigations on heat producting plants|journal=Thermochimica Acta|year=2002|volume=391|issue=1–2 |pages=107–118|doi=10.1016/s0040-6031(02)00168-5}}</ref>

==Cytology==
The diploid chromosome count of ''Victoria cruziana'' is 2n = 24.<ref name = "Pellicer et al., 2013">{{cite journal | url=https://cdnsciencepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1139/gen-2013-0039?download=true | doi=10.1139/gen-2013-0039 | title=Insights into the dynamics of genome size and chromosome evolution in the early diverging angiosperm lineage Nymphaeales (Water lilies) | date=2013 | last1=Pellicer | first1=J. | last2=Kelly | first2=L.J. | last3=Magdalena | first3=C. | last4=Leitch | first4=I.J. | journal=Genome | volume=56 | issue=8 | pages=437–449 | pmid=24168627 }}</ref> The chloroplast genome is 158993 bp long.<ref name = "Gruenstaeudl et al., 2017">Gruenstaeudl, M., Nauheimer, L., & Borsch, T. (2017). [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318253682_Plastid_genome_structure_and_phylogenomics_of_Nymphaeales_conserved_gene_order_and_new_insights_into_relationships Plastid genome structure and phylogenomics of Nymphaeales: conserved gene order and new insights into relationships.] Plant systematics and evolution, 303, 1251-1270.</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Victoria cruziana'' was discovered in Bolivia on one of many expeditions through the country by [[Alcide d'Orbigny]] whose presence was sponsored by [[Andrés de Santa Cruz]]. The first collected specimens were returned to [[France]] where they were named in honor of Santa Cruz by Alcide's brother, [[Charles Henry Dessalines d'Orbigny]].{{Citation needed|date=June 2013}}

It was first described in 1840 by Alcide d'Orbigny in Annales des Sciences Naturelles; Botanique, Ser. 2, 13, p. 57.<ref name="Tropicos c479">{{cite web | title=Tropicos | website=Tropicos | url=https://www.tropicos.org/Name/22600197 | access-date=2023-08-29}}</ref> Synonyms for ''Victoria cruziana'' A.D.Orb. are: ''Victoria argentina'' Burmeist. noun nud., ''Victoria cruziana'' var. ''malmei'' F.Henkel et al., ''Victoria cruziana'' f. ''matogrossensis'' Malme, ''Victoria cruziana'' f. ''trickeri'' F.Henkel ex Malme, ''Victoria cruziana'' var. ''trickeri'' F.Henkel et al., ''Victoria regia'' var (A.D.Orb.) C.Lawson, ''Victoria trickeri'' (F.Henkel ex Malme) hort. ex Mutzek.
